analysis.title: The AI boom learns to do the math
key_insights: UBS CIO's Varnholt argues rising stock markets and falling valuations are not a contradiction. The Nasdaq 100 rose from 23,481 at the start of the year to 25,618, while its P/E ratio fell about 20%, because earnings (the denominator) are rising faster than prices.

The report says the current market differs from the dotcom bubble: major tech companies are generating record cash flows, not just narratives. At the 2000 peak the Nasdaq 100 had a triple-digit P/E, and AOL traded at about 197x in the Time Warner deal.

The report views pullbacks as more likely buying opportunities than the start of a crash, citing strong earnings growth, structural investment momentum and robust macro data. It says euphoria, not fear, creates bubbles, and that it is far from euphoria today given the gap between prices and earnings.

Forward S&P 500 EPS rose from USD 147 four years ago to USD 366 for this year. Analysts expect USD 425 next year. Earnings growth this year is 31%, while the index is up just under 10% as of 2 November, so many markets have become cheaper.

The cheapening is not only a US effect. In Japan, emerging markets and Europe, earnings growth also exceeds market gains. The MSCI EMU trades at a P/E of 13.9x and the MSCI EM at 8.9x, both well below levels at the start of the year.

Analysts expect revenue and earnings growth in all 11 S&P 500 sectors in 3Q26. That would be only the second time since 2000, after the quarter following the lockdowns. They expect 2026 aggregate revenue growth of 11.6% and earnings growth of 30.6% for the S&P 500.

US semiconductors account for about one-fifth of US corporate operating earnings but trade at a forward P/E of 13.5x versus 18.5x for the S&P 500. Analysts expect annualized five-year earnings growth of 25.6% for the S&P 500, 41.9% for IT and 66.0% for semiconductors. Investors doubt these rates because competition rises where profits are large.

BEA data show US pretax profits up about sixfold since 2000 to USD 4.7 trillion annualized, and after-tax profits at USD 3.9 trillion. Profits are just under 18% of national income, a record, versus about 10% in 2000. The wage share fell from 66% to about 60%.

Companies hold about USD 1.7 trillion of profits on balance sheets, and about USD 1.2 trillion of US profits were earned abroad. UBS says productivity growth underpins its 'Roaring Twenties' scenario and protects against inflation and higher rates.

Last week's tech sell-off hit China's Star 50 index, down more than 40% over four months, and the Nasdaq 100, more than 10% below its peak. Major tech stocks were also hit when strong earnings growth fell short of higher expectations.

The report cites a reported theft of about USD 6.5 billion from the crypto exchange Binance this week, which it calls the largest digital bank robbery in history. Hackers reportedly used AI. It notes that decentralized crypto still depends on centralized exchanges. UBS argues the episode may push investors to demand higher risk premiums and focus on protected earnings.

sector_views.rationale: The report says the sector is about one-fifth of US operating earnings but trades at a forward P/E of 13.5x versus 18.5x for the S&P 500, with analysts expecting 66.0% annualized five-year earnings growth. It does not give an explicit rating.
The report expects 41.9% annualized five-year earnings growth for the IT sector. It treats the recent sell-off as a likely buying opportunity but gives no formal sector rating.

earnings_insights: Analysts (consensus) expect 2026 S&P 500 earnings growth of 30.6% and revenue growth of 11.6%. The report also cites 31% earnings growth this year against forward EPS of USD 366 (estimate).
Consensus for 3Q26 is simultaneous revenue and earnings growth in all 11 S&P 500 sectors. The report says this would be only the second such quarter since 2000.
Analyst consensus for next-year S&P 500 EPS is USD 425, against USD 366 for this year (forward estimates).

macro_indicators.interpretation: Profits are about sixfold the 2000 level and just under 18% of national income, a record.

macro_indicators.indicator: Wage share of US national income
macro_indicators.interpretation: Down from 66% in 2000 as profits take a larger share, which the report links to productivity growth.
Analyst expectation, far above the index's roughly 10% price gain, so valuations have compressed.

crypto_views: Hackers reportedly stole about USD 6.5 billion from the crypto exchange Binance this week, which the report calls the largest digital bank robbery in history.
The report says the theft shows decentralized blockchain currencies depend on centralized exchanges and are vulnerable to a 'once-in-a-century heist'.
The report says the hackers used AI to gain access.
UBS suggests the episode may lead decision-makers to strengthen security and demand higher risk premiums, which could constrain cybercrime and euphoric bubble formation.
risk_factors: Competitive pressure typically rises where profits are large, which may threaten the growth rates analysts expect for semiconductors.
Tech earnings that grow strongly but miss higher expectations can still trigger sell-offs.
Cybersecurity and centralized-exchange risk in crypto, as shown by the reported Binance theft.
The report notes that bubbles form in euphoria, and that investors who believe they have found a new economic law have preceded every major bubble.
vol_and_positioning: The report notes that investor skepticism toward the earnings surge 'primarily makes markets more resilient'.
The Nasdaq 100 is more than 10% below its peak after last week's tech sell-off.
geopolitical: The report recalls 'Liberation Day' on 5 April 2025, when Trump's tariff announcement triggered a decline of up to 12% in the S&P 500.

tension_points.bull_case: UBS says earnings growth of about 31% far outpaces the index's roughly 10% gain, so P/E ratios have fallen, and tech firms generate record cash flows, unlike in the dotcom era.
tension_points.bear_case: Tech stocks sold off last week even on strong earnings that missed higher expectations. Investors doubt the growth rates because competition rises where profits are large.
tension_points.what_invalidates: The report names no specific level. It says bubbles form in euphoria, which it does not see today given the gap between prices and earnings.

theme_stances.key_argument: The bull market is driven by rising earnings (the P/E denominator), not rising valuations, so the setup differs from the dotcom bubble.
theme_stances.evidence: differences between now and then are greater than the similarities
